turns.user: Explain why a lock prevents two writers from colliding.
turns.assistant:
Loading the communication profile, then answering in that style.**Answer**
A lock lets only one writer change shared data at a time.

**Why**
Without a lock, two writers can change the same data together.
Their updates can mix, or one update can wipe the other.
A lock is a short-term claim on that data.
The writer that holds it may write; others must wait.
When that writer finishes, it drops the lock so the next may write.
Writers never change the same data at the same moment.

**Example**
Two apps save the same file.
The first takes the lock, writes, then releases it.
The second waits, then writes after the first is done.
